dod_intent_evidence: AFWERX Direct-to-Phase II Space Force SBIR contract ($1,246,661, 2023) for on-orbit cloud computing 'closing the kill web faster' per the SBIR abstract and News section (AccessNewswire, Nov 2023).
score_evidence: 'Empower The Universe With Information... We deliver unparalleled high-performance computing capabilities to space' → lab_language_intensity
'Data Centers will be in space by 2027' with zero ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR language anywhere despite an active DoD Space Force contract → deployment_awareness_absence

'Nebula's Executive Team is comprised of industry experts driven by enthusiasm and an entrepreneurial spirit' — no operator, warfighter, or field-feedback language anywhere on the site → operator_absence

Five 'sister companies' (Fabrx, Nebula Cybersecurity, Nebula Compute, Nebula Incubator, Nebula Media) claiming to 'achieve secure superiority in space' run by a 4-5 person team holding one Direct-to-Phase II award → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Promises 'data-center-grade' on-orbit servers with zero discussion of the actual space environment's power/thermal/radiation constraints
blind_spots.operator_reality: SWaP-C in space is not optional — launch mass, power budget, and radiation hardening determine whether 'data-center-grade' compute is even physically possible on orbit; the site never engages with this, only the end-state vision
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: messaging is entirely aspirational/pre-launch ('Data Centers will be in space by 2027') with no visible hardware engineering detail
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We deliver unparalleled high-performance computing capabilities to space

blind_spots.blind_spot: NebuCyber sister company claims to 'deliver managed space security operations for Department of Defense capabilities on Nebula Compute Contracts' with zero ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR mention anywhere in the corporate family
blind_spots.operator_reality: A company handling DoD compute and cybersecurity workloads must clear security accreditation before any operational unit can trust it with data — silence on this while claiming DoD-facing contracts across five entities is the exact 'dead transition' risk pattern
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: corporate structure emphasizes vision and advisor pedigree (retired generals, an astronaut) over a visible compliance or ISSO function
blind_spots.evidence_quote: NebuCyber delivers managed space security operations for Department of Defense capabilities on Nebula Compute Contracts

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Space-based and quantum powered' cybersecurity claims for a company whose core compute product hasn't launched
blind_spots.operator_reality: Unfalsifiable lab-brag layered onto pre-product hardware means an operator evaluating this for the 'kill web' has no way to validate performance claims before committing program funding and schedule to it
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: advisory board is stacked with credibility (Lt. Gen., astronaut, space-industry veterans) that substitutes for demonstrated technical readiness
blind_spots.evidence_quote: NebuCyber is space-based and quantum powered with more sensor data, computing power, and accuracy than competitors in the industry

opener_hook: Nebula Compute's AFWERX Direct-to-Phase II Space Force contract targets 'closing the kill web faster' — worth asking how a still-pre-launch on-orbit server clears an ATO before the 2027 target.
what_they_do: Developing on-orbit cloud computing servers (ServerSats) to bring data-center-grade compute to space under a Space Force AFWERX Direct-to-Phase II SBIR contract, alongside four other 'sister companies' spanning cybersecurity, blockchain-based space data infrastructure, media, and an incubator.
